newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada spending on tourism rises in Q1.
newsitem.headline: Canada spending on tourism rises in Q1.

text.p: Spending on tourism in Canada rose 2.9 percent in the first quarter of 1997 compared to the same period a year earlier, Statistics Canada said on Friday.
Tourism spending totaled C$10.6 billion in the quarter, a rise of 0.7 percent from C$10.5 billion in the fourth quarter of 1996, StatsCan said.
For the year of 1996, total tourism spending reached a record C$41.8 billion, up 4.7 percent from C$39.9 billion in 1995, the agency said.
During the first quarter, visitors from other countries spent a seasonally adjusted C$3.1 billion, up 1.6 percent from the previous quarter.
Canadians spent C$7.5 billion on tourism in Canada, a rise of 0.3 percent from the fourth quarter.
For the year of 1996, foreigners spent C$12.1 billion, up 10.4 percent from 1995, while Canadians spent C$29.7 billion in Canada, up 2.6 percent from 1995.
